title: Boom Selection
label: Incentive (Kronik)

type.basis: A garage-rap chart hit; sources call it UK garage and place it before the grimy era. Held as an outgroup.

sound.text: Wikipedia notes its sample of 'Gravedigger' by the New York Rock & Roll Ensemble; no further sound description was found.

context.text: Official Singles Chart peak no. 12 (first chart date 3 Feb 2001); Dance chart no. 1 (2 weeks at the top, 11 weeks in all).

Reynolds (2015, reusing his 2013 Wire Grime Primer) calls it 'the immortal Boom Selection' and places Genius Cru's playful bonhomie just before the grimy era; he treats garage rap as a flavour of 2-step and UKG.

calls.label: garage rap (a subset of 2-step/UKG), pre-'grimy era'
calls.source: Simon Reynolds, blissblog (Grime Primer material from 2013)

uncertainty: This is the weakest bridge record in the batch. Every source calls it UK garage; Reynolds sets it just before grime but does not call it grime or proto-grime, and gives no sound description. Kept as a garage-side control for the register's genre-call comparison; drop it if the register wants only records tied to grime by name.
tracklist: 12-inch: A1 Original Vocal Mix; A2 Bulletproof Dub; AA1 Gridlock Remix; the CD adds the video. Samples 'Gravedigger' by the New York Rock & Roll Ensemble.
